correctness.rationale: The four-state digit automaton is equivalent to the Baum–Sweet zero-run rule; exhaustive closure proves exactly eight adjacent substitution pairs; every factor of length at most 8192 is covered by their 2^13-substituted coded blocks. Eertree enumerates all literal nonzero palindromes, zero words appear from DD, and assertions check each of 8192 lengths. A separate center-expansion check matches full literal palindrome sets through 128, and the program verifies the first 8192 sequence digits.

Specific Baum–Sweet queries of the published-record search and literature did not find any stated or stronger covering table. This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness proof; an unindexed prior table remains possible.

value.rationale: Palindrome complexity is a standard, motivated measure for an automatic word, and Baum–Sweet is a classical nonprimitive four-state 2-automatic example with a structurally unusual long-run distribution. A complete exact finite profile through 8192, with 66 nontrivial dyadic exceptions, supplies a concrete benchmark of factor symmetry and nontrivial sparse regularity invisible in general existence theorems. This is much more than a small incremental suffix count, while no infinite extension is claimed.
